record.paper_title: Selection Principles in Mathematics: A Milestone of Open Problems
record.original_question: For a space X, call X a δ-set when every open ω-cover U of X has X in L(U), where L(U) is the closure of U under the operation lim inf applied to sequences of subsets. Call X a γ-set when every open ω-cover contains an infinite subcover in which each point of X belongs to all but finitely many members. Is the δ-property equivalent to the γ-property?

evidence.quote: X is a δ-set (or: has the δ-property) if for each ω -cover U of X, X ∈ L(U). Observe that if {Un}n∈ N is a γ-cover of X, then X = lim inf Un. Thus, the γ-property implies the δ-property. Surprisingly, the converse is still open.
Problem 12.1 ([22, p. 160]) . Is the δ-property equivalent to the γ-property?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a topological space. An open cover U of X is called an ω-cover if X is not a member of U and for every finite subset F ⊆ X there exists U ∈ U with F ⊆ U. An infinite open cover {U_n : n ∈ ℕ} of X is called a γ-cover if every point x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many of the sets U_n. 

For a family U of subsets of X, define L(U) to be the smallest family containing U that is closed under the operation of taking lim inf of sequences, where for a sequence (A_n) of subsets of X one sets liminf_n A_n = ⋃_{n} ⋂_{k ≥ n} A_k.

Call X a δ-set if for every open ω-cover U of X one has X ∈ L(U). Call X a γ-set if every open ω-cover of X contains a countably infinite subfamily that is a γ-cover of X (equivalently, every open ω-cover has an infinite subcover such that each point of X lies in all but finitely many members).

Since any γ-cover {U_n} satisfies X = liminf_n U_n, the γ-property implies the δ-property.

Question: Is the δ-property equivalent to the γ-property? That is, must every δ-set be a γ-set?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in standard surveys of open problems in selection principles (Tsaban's milestone problem list and the follow-up "Selection principles and special sets of reals: open problems"). No publicly available source indicates that the equivalence between the δ-property and the γ-property has been settled; subsequent surveys continue to list it among the open problems concerning ω-covers and γ-covers.
